result.target_topic: Indebtedness, Refinancing, and Covenant Compliance Risks
result.target_summary: NVIDIA has $9.7 billion in net outstanding notes due by 2060 and a $575 million commercial paper program. Risks include adverse effects on financial position from indebtedness, inability to refinance on favorable terms, and debt service obligations limiting operational flexibility. Additionally, the company may breach indenture covenants due to events beyond its control, causing indebtedness to become immediately due, while changes in credit rating could negatively impact security value, liquidity, and future financing abilities.

comparisons.peer_topic: Debt Covenants and Credit Agreement Restrictions
comparisons.peer_summary: The indentures governing AMD's senior notes and the Assumed Xilinx Notes, along with its $3.0 billion Revolving Credit Agreement, impose covenants that restrict AMD's ability to incur liens, enter into sale-leaseback transactions, merge, or sell substantially all assets. The Revolving Credit Agreement also requires maintenance of a minimum interest coverage ratio and includes cross-default provisions that could accelerate debt repayment if AMD defaults on other material indebtedness, creating liquidity risk if lenders accelerate borrowings.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD disclose specific risks related to debt covenant compliance and the restrictive nature of their credit agreements and indentures. NVIDIA warns that events beyond its control could affect its ability to comply with covenants in its indenture, potentially causing indebtedness to become immediately due, while also noting that maintenance of indebtedness restricts operational flexibility regarding mergers, asset disposals, and granting liens. Similarly, AMD details that its indentures and Revolving Credit Agreement impose restrictions limiting its ability to create liens, enter into sale-leaseback transactions, or merge and sell substantially all assets. Both companies highlight that these covenants restrict corporate actions and could limit financial flexibility, though NVIDIA specifically emphasizes the risk of covenants being affected by events beyond control, whereas AMD explicitly lists the specific prohibited transactions like liens and mergers in the context of the agreement restrictions.

sentences.text: Our ability to comply with the covenants in our indenture may be affected by events beyond our control.

Maintenance of our current and future indebtedness and contractual restrictions could cause us to dedicate a substantial portion of our cash flows from operations towards debt service obligations and principal repayments; increase our vulnerability to adverse changes in general economic, industry and competitive conditions; limit our flexibility regarding changes in our business and our industry; impair our ability to obtain future financing; and restrict our ability to grant liens on property, enter into certain mergers, dispose of our assets, or materially change our business.

The indenture governing our 3.924% Senior Notes due 2032 and 4.393% Senior Notes due 2052 contains various covenants that limit our ability to, among other things: create liens on certain assets to secure debt, enter into certain sale and leaseback transactions; and consolidate with, merge into or sell, convey or lease all or substantially all of our assets to any other person.

The agreements governing our notes, our guarantee of the Assumed Xilinx Notes, and our Revolving Credit Agreement impose restrictions on us that may adversely affect our ability to operate our business.
